title: 舟夜书所见
titleEn: What I Saw from a Boat at Night
author: 查慎行
intro: A tiny night scene in twenty characters: one fishing lamp on a dark river, a breath of wind — and suddenly the whole river is full of stars.
analysis: 题目的意思是“在船上过夜，写下看到的景色”。前两句写静：没有月亮的黑夜里，只看见远处一盏渔船上的灯，孤零零的一点光，像一只萤火虫。后两句写动：微风吹来，水面泛起细细的波浪，灯光的倒影被打碎，散开来，变成满河的星星。一盏灯变成满河星，从“一点”到“满河”，从静到动，画面一下子亮了起来。诗人用了两个比喻：把灯光比作萤火，把碎开的倒影比作星星。“簇”字很传神，写出风把浪推成一小堆一小堆的样子。这首诗没有讲什么大道理，只是把一瞬间的美景准确地抓住了，语言简单，非常适合初学者读。
analysisEn: The title simply means “spending the night on a boat, writing down what I saw”. The first two lines are still: on a moonless night, all he can see is one lamp on a distant fishing boat, a single point of light like a firefly. The last two lines move: a light breeze ruffles the water into little waves, and the lamp’s reflection breaks apart and scatters into a river full of stars. One light becomes countless lights; stillness becomes motion; the dark picture suddenly sparkles. The poet uses two comparisons — the lamp is a firefly, and its broken reflection is a sky of stars on the water. The verb 簇 (“to bunch up”) is precise: the wind pushes the water into small clustered ripples. There is no big message here, just one beautiful moment caught exactly as it happened. The vocabulary is simple, which makes it a lovely first poem for learners — and a good reminder that 见 (“to see”) and 星 (“star”) haven’t changed in three hundred years.
background: Zha Shenxing (1650–1727) was an early Qing poet from Haining, Zhejiang, admired for his fresh, precise descriptions of scenery. He spent many years travelling, and this poem records a night on a boat.
pronunciation: 查 zhā（姓氏，不读 chá）。见 jiàn。簇 cù。散 sàn（散开，不读 sǎn）。
version: 采用通行文本，已与维基文库本（出《他山诗钞》）核对一致。

lines.lit: The moon dark, I see a fisherman’s lamp:
lines.en: No moon tonight — just one fishing lamp,

lines.lit: a lone light, one dot like a firefly.
lines.en: a lonely glow, small as a firefly.

lines.lit: Gently, the wind bunches up the waves,
lines.en: A soft wind gathers the water into ripples,

lines.lit: scattering it into a river full of stars.
lines.en: and the light breaks into a river of stars.

words.note: 古义“写”，今天“书写”“书法”还保留这个意思。
现代汉语常用，如“微微一笑”。

imagery.name: 灯
imagery.zh: 黑夜里一盏孤零零的渔灯，是全诗唯一的光。
imagery.en: One lonely fishing lamp in the dark — the only light in the poem.

imagery.name: 星
imagery.zh: 灯影被风浪打碎，变成满河星星，一点光化成无数光。
imagery.en: The wind breaks the lamp’s reflection into a riverful of stars — one light becomes countless.
